steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“Today” is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Six days from today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The time given is 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time), which in late October is usually PDT (UTC−7). Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2). The time difference is 9 hours ahead in Madrid, so 11:59 PM PT becomes 08:59 AM the next day in Madrid.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid uses Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) on 2026-10-30.  
Los Angeles on that date is on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7). The time difference is 9 hours (LA behind Madrid).  
So “Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time” is 19:00 (7:00 PM) in Madrid on Monday 2026-11-02.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) on October 24, 2026 (DST ends later that year on the last Sunday of October).  
Start: Saturday 2026-10-24 18:00.  
Duration: 48 hours → end at 2026-10-26 18:00 (local time).

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

10:00 AM PT on 2026-10-26 corresponds to 7:00 PM in Madrid on 2026-10-26 (Spain is on CEST, UTC+2, while PT is PDT, UTC-7; the difference is +9 hours). Submissions close 72 hours later, i.e., 7:00 PM on 2026-10-29.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close on **October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET**. Madrid is on **CEST (UTC+2)** during late October 2026, while ET is **EDT (UTC-4)**, so the time difference is **6 hours**.  
Convert close time: 11:59 PM ET → **5:59 AM** on **Nov 1, 2026** in Madrid.  
Results are announced **exactly 36 hours** later: 5:59 AM + 36 hours = **5:59 PM** on **Nov 2, 2026** in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Unix timestamp **1791788340** corresponds to **2026-10-10 13:19** in **Tokyo (JST, UTC+9)**.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:19 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Time (CEST) in late October (UTC+2). The deadline `2026-10-25T02:30:00Z` converts to `2026-10-25 04:30` in local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026 is **Sunday, October 25, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT**. In Madrid (CET/CEST), that date is under **CEST (UTC+2)** while PT is **UTC−7**, so the time difference is **+9 hours**. Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM gives **8:59 AM on Monday, October 26, 2026** local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, the US ends daylight saving time on **Sunday, November 1**. The deadline is **12:00 noon Eastern Time** on that date, which is **UTC−5** after the shift (EST). Lima (Peru) is **UTC−5 year-round**, so the time matches local time.  

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“AoE” means Anywhere on Earth, i.e., the latest time zone covered by the contest’s day—commonly interpreted as UTC−12:00.  
So December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE corresponds to **January 1, 2027, 12:00 JST** in Tokyo (JST = UTC+09:00, a 21-hour difference from UTC−12:00).

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 12:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid uses Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in early October. Sydney uses Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT, UTC+11) on October 5, 2026. The time difference is 9 hours, with Sydney ahead of Madrid.

So, 5:00 PM (17:00) Sydney time on 2026-10-05 corresponds to 08:00 AM (08:00) in Madrid on 2026-10-05.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 08:00
